explanations.deployment_assurance_scalability: The comment argues that the same function carries materially different risk depending on the local deployment context (e.g., populations with ready specialty access versus none), implying risk and assurance cannot be settled once centrally but must account for variation across deployment environments.
explanations.human_ai_system_performance: The point that duration and accumulation of reliance can compound error into a user's settled belief frames risk as a property of the evolving human-device interaction rather than of device output accuracy alone.

explanations.evidence_burden_commercial_viability: The comment frames classification ambiguity as a burden that falls disproportionately on small sponsors who cannot absorb the cost of discovering their risk classification only after a deficiency letter, urging pre-development clarity through published worked examples.

explanations.human_ai_system_performance: The comment argues that "talk to your doctor" boilerplate is not a genuine mitigation and that in DGBI most patients receive no professional input at all, so evaluation cannot assume a clinician backstop in the human-AI use pathway and must instead reckon with the realistic alternative (unaided search and social content).

explanations.dynamic_intended_use: By insisting that credit be given only for verifiable behavioral properties—structurally non-directive framing, forced deferral on treatment-change requests, bidirectional escalation scaffolding—demonstrated under adversarial testing, the comment reframes patient-facing risk control as constraining and evidencing the device's behavioral envelope rather than relying on a static intended-use statement plus disclaimers.

The comment proposes defining intended use for conversational devices via a testable "conversational envelope" of prohibited behaviors across trajectories, directly raising the need for a behavioral-envelope conception of intended use rather than static per-turn labeling.

explanations.evidence_burden_commercial_viability: The comment argues that requiring prospective trials for every conversational function would impose costs only large incumbents can bear, consolidating the market and preventing low-risk beneficial products from ever being built—an access and viability concern beyond Q11's framing of proportionate confirmation methods.

The comment argues that imposing an evidentiary/performance standard higher than the existing delivery system on low-risk educational software yields no protective benefit and instead keeps such products from reaching patients who currently have no alternative, raising the cross-cutting concern that disproportionate evidence burdens block viable beneficial offerings.

explanations.deployment_assurance_scalability: The comment locates assurance in deployed-use instrumentation—automated drift surveillance, sampled independent adjudication, reporting cadence, and rollback capability—arguing that real deployment generates more decision-relevant evidence than any premarket sample, which goes beyond FDA's framing of postmarket monitoring as merely a substitute for premarket evidence.

explanations.ai_supplier_quality: The comment centers on the quality and transparency obligations of upstream foundation model suppliers, proposing version pinning, deprecation timelines, update notification commitments, and healthcare-relevant evaluation summaries as MAF content.
explanations.distributed_accountability: It highlights that a small manufacturer bears regulatory responsibility yet lacks contractual leverage over the model developer, so accountability is split unevenly across the supply chain and concentrated with the largest sponsors.
explanations.deployment_assurance_scalability: The proposed sponsor-side re-benchmarking gate—no underlying model change enters production until the full premarket benchmark battery is re-run and passed—raises the question of how repeated revalidation can be sustained at the pace of upstream model updates.

explanations.ai_supplier_quality: The comment proposes converting an uncontrollable third-party foundation model dependency into an auditable, prespecified re-benchmarking and PCCP-governed change process within the sponsor's quality system, i.e., a supplier-quality control mechanism for externally initiated model updates.

explanations.evidence_burden_commercial_viability: The comment warns that third-party certification fees and access terms could act as a toll gate affordable only to incumbents, raising cost-of-evidence barriers for smaller sponsors beyond FDA's framing.
